title: Two rollers on the rim of a fixed disk, rolling apart at omega and 2 omega: rolling without slipping, the centres' circle R + r and the time until they touch again
summary: Two small disks touching on the rim of a clamped disk roll apart at omega and 2 omega. Magnifying lenses show each contact point at rest and v = omega r; the centres ride on the circle R + r, so they go round at omega/51 and 2 omega/51; a stopwatch times the long way round until the centres are again 2r apart, and all four options are audited.
subject: Physics
chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
topic: Rolling without slipping on a fixed circular surface - angular speed of the centre and relative angular motion
subtopics: Rolling without slipping: the contact point is instantaneously at rest, v = omega r
Rolling on the outside of a fixed circle: the centre moves on radius R + r
Coin-rotation paradox: a roller spins 1 + R/r times per lap
Relative angular motion of two bodies moving round a circle in opposite directions
Contact angle between two touching disks on a circle (small-angle approximation)
concepts: The contact point of a disk rolling on a fixed surface is at rest, so its centre moves at v = omega r
Rolling round the outside of a fixed disk, the centre is at distance R + r from O, so Omega = omega r/(R + r) = omega/51, not omega/50
Moving in opposite directions, the angle between the centres changes at Omega1 + Omega2 = 3 omega/51
Touching disks of finite size meet again when the far-side gap closes to the contact angle: the sweep is 2 pi - 2 dTheta, not 2 pi
With sin dTheta = dTheta the chord 2r equals the arc (R + r) dTheta, so dTheta = 2/51
formulas: v = omega r (rolling without slipping on a fixed surface)

methods: Solved independently from the rolling constraint and the geometry: Omega = omega r/(R + r), dTheta = 2r/(R + r), sweep 2 pi - 2 dTheta, tau = 51(2 pi - 4/51)/3 omega - option C
sympy: only option C simplifies to the derived tau
RK4 time stepping of both centres by the no-slip condition alone (contact material point at rest), exact contact angle: omega tau = 105.4807, within 0.01 % of C
Coin rotation: integrated spin 51 turns per lap; roller 2 spins twice as far as roller 1
Controls R/r = 10, 5; speeds (1,1), (1,3), (2,3): all follow (R + r)/r (2 pi - 2 dTheta)/(n1 + n2)
Every option audited: A uses omega/51 for the relative speed, B removes dTheta once, D both
